 Blog Torino Film Festival 2026: dates, tickets and sources
 Official dates of the Torino Film Festival 2026, press accreditation before 30 October, venues and reference ticket prices, with their sources.
 October 23, 2026 
 15 min 
 Read article 
 Magazine 
 Table of Contents
 Loading... 
 Commercial partnership · This article contains affiliate links. If you book through these links, Pixidia earns a small commission at no extra cost to you.
 Learn more The Torino Film Festival 2026 runs from 24 November to 2 December 2026 in Turin. The opening ceremony is at the Teatro Regio, and the full programme will be presented in Rome on 5 November 2026. No 2026 ticket prices are published yet: the reference is the 2025 full ticket, €7.50.
 Checked on 23 October 2026 against the official sources cited (torinofilmfest.org, gov.uk). 
 The 44th edition of the Torino Film Festival lasts nine days. This guide separates what the organiser has confirmed from what is still to be confirmed, flags the deadlines that already matter to journalists and industry professionals, and explains how to plan a trip while the 2026 programme and prices are still unpublished. Everything below is dated 23 October 2026.
 1. Where the Torino Film Festival takes place
Photo by Marcus Ganahl 
on Unsplash Museo Nazionale del Cinema, Mole Antonelliana
 City centre, Turin 
 Festival from 24 November to 2 December 2026 
 2026 tickets not yet published 
 19th-century monument The National Museum of Cinema occupies the Mole Antonelliana, the landmark that dominates the city and that Turin locals use as their reference point. The organiser presents the museum as the institutional home of the edition: the museum’s festival lab names it as the festival’s base. It is therefore the place to start if you want to understand the event, even though the 2026 screening venues have not been announced yet.
 What to know
 The museum is presented as the festival’s institutional home; the 2026 screening venues are not confirmed yet. 
 The guided visit lasts 2 hours according to the Viator listing and includes the panoramic climb up the Mole. 
 The meeting point is the museum entrance. Latecomers are not admitted, so arrive on time. 
 Pixidia tip: plan a backup for the panoramic climb. According to the Viator listing, the climb is not guaranteed in bad weather; the visit may then be limited to the museum. 
 Semi-private guided tour of the National Museum of Cinema and Mole Antonelliana 
 2 hours · ★ 4.5 out of 5 ( 15 reviews, Viator and TripAdvisor) 
Book my guided tour 
 The Teatro Regio hosts the opening ceremony. The two venues need different preparation: the museum visit is a fixed two-hour slot with a guide, while the ceremony depends on a start time and access arrangements that have not been published yet.
 2. The 2026 calendar: the dates to note
 The festival runs for nine days, from Tuesday 24 November to Wednesday 2 December 2026. The organiser confirms these dates on its official website, unless the table says otherwise.
 Key dates of the Torino Film Festival 2026 and the status of each one Date Event Status 
 Friday 30 October 2026, 12:00 pm (time not confirmed by the organiser) Press accreditation request deadline Official 
 Tuesday 3 November 2026 Press fee: €60 up to 3 November, €70 after Official 
 Thursday 5 November 2026 Press conference in Rome, full programme Official 
 Tuesday 24 November 2026 Opening ceremony at the Teatro Regio (time not published) Official (venue and host) 
 Thursday 26 to Monday 30 November 2026 Torino Film Industry, the industry market Secondary source, to be reconfirmed 
 Wednesday 2 December 2026 Festival closing Official 
 Source: torinofilmfest.org , checked on 23 October 2026; market dates: Italy Meets Hollywood , checked on 23 October 2026. 
 The most pressing deadline is not the opening but 30 October. A journalist or photographer preparing coverage has to file the request twenty-five days before the festival’s first day. The full programme only becomes public on 5 November, nineteen days before the opening: if you want to see specific films, you will need to choose quickly.
 3. Tickets: what is published and what is not
 As of 23 October 2026, the organiser’s homepage shows no ticket sales call for the 2026 edition, and no ticket price appears there. Writing a 2026 price today would mean inventing a figure. The only published reference is the 2025 edition: full ticket €7.50, reduced ticket €5.50, and the TFF Pass at €110 (organiser’s 2025 ticketing information, checked on 23 October 2026). These are not 2026 prices; the table in section 7 sets them beside other costs.
 Two cautions apply. First, the 2025 pass does not predict the 2026 price. Second, popular screenings sell out quickly, as the 2025 figures in section 5 show, so choose early.
 4. Press, industry and photographer accreditation
 The organiser runs three separate forms: press, industry professionals (the Torino Film Industry market) and photographers or camera operators. For the press, the request must be filed by Friday 30 October 2026 at 12:00 pm, Turin time (time not confirmed by the organiser). The fee is €60 before 3 November and €70 after (press accreditation page, checked on 23 October 2026).
 Accreditation is for journalists, pubblicisti (a registered category of Italian freelance journalists) and press officers; it is granted by professional category and at the festival’s discretion. The pages we checked do not explain how hybrid cases are handled, such as a content creator who publishes for a media outlet and for their own audience. The safest step is to ask for written confirmation before you pay.
 If you are covering the festival, file your request before 30 October 2026.
 5. What the figures from the 43rd edition show
 Attendance at the 43rd Torino Film Festival (November to December 2025) Indicator 2025 value 
 Average seat occupancy 83%, so 17% of seats free on average 
 Sold-out screenings 65 
 Source: Cinemaitaliano, final report of 3 December 2025 . Checked on 23 October 2026. 
 What this means for you: with 65 sold-out screenings, the challenge is less getting a seat than choosing early the screenings you want. The report does not say which screenings were full. For films you really want to see, aim for the first screening of the day and keep a second option.
 6. Getting to Turin: entry and transport
Photo by Nikolai Kolosov 
on Unsplash Entering Italy and reaching the centre
 Passport issued in the last 10 years 
 No visa for stays up to 90 days 
 Porta Nuova and Porta Susa 
 Turin-Caselle airport (TRN) For a British passport holder, no visa is needed for a stay of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area, which includes Italy. Your passport must have been issued less than 10 years before your arrival, and must expire at least three months after the day you plan to leave the Schengen area. The UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office travel advice for Italy, checked on 23 October 2026, sets out these rules: entry requirements for Italy . On your first entry you may also be asked to register your fingerprints and photo under the EU’s Entry/Exit System (EES), at no charge. ETIAS, the EU online travel authorisation planned for UK visitors, has no confirmed start date in the sources we checked, so look at the official EU website before you travel.
 What to check before you leave
 Your passport’s issue date and expiry, checked before you book your ticket, not on the day you travel. 
 Train times and fares to Porta Nuova or Porta Susa, which we did not check for this article. 
 Local transport fares, to check on the GTT website on the date of your trip. 
 Pixidia tip: the transfer from Caselle airport to the city centre is one of the least documented points in this guide. The official airport page we checked describes no transfer service, and the only shuttle announcement we found dates from 2019. Compare the options for your travel date rather than relying on an old fare. Torino Porta Nuova and Torino Porta Susa are presented as the city’s two main rail arrival points. Press coverage mentions connections from Paris and Milan, whose timetables and fares we did not check here. Travelling from London? The Eurostar gets you to Paris, from where you continue by rail; undated travel guides put the whole trip at roughly 10 to 11 hours with a change. Check 2026 timetables with the operators before you book. We did not check the walking time from each station to the centre either: allow for it with a mapping app on arrival day.
 If you travel with a mobility app, think about the bus and tram network too. GTT tickets are described on third-party sites, but we found no dated fare in this research: check the official source before you leave.
 7. Budget: a range without 2026 prices
 Without a published 2026 ticket, the budget is built around costs sourced at a given date. The table separates what has been checked from what remains indicative or unchecked.
 Budget items for a trip to the Torino Film Festival (checked on 23 October 2026; 2026 not published unless stated) Item Amount or benchmark Status 
 Screening ticket, full €7.50 in 2025 Not published for 2026; 2025 reference 
 Screening ticket, reduced €5.50 in 2025 Not published for 2026; 2025 reference 
 Festival pass €110 in 2025 Not published for 2026; 2025 reference 
 Press accreditation €60 before 3 November, €70 after Official; press accreditation page 
 Museum admission without the guided tour not checked with certainty Admission is included in the Viator tour 
 Train from Paris or Milan to Turin not checked Timetables and fares to check with the operators 
 Caselle to city centre transfer not checked (only announcement found: 2019) Compare for your travel date 
 GTT tickets (bus and tram) not checked Check on the GTT website 
 Hostel bed from €20 a night Indicative, outside the festival (Hostelworld listing) 
 B&B room up to €58 a night Indicative, outside the festival (Hostelworld listing) 
 Sources: torinofilmfest.org, 2025 ticketing information ; press accreditation page ; Hostelworld listing (indicative accommodation, not linked to the festival). Checked on 23 October 2026. 
 The Viator listing says the tour takes up to 15 people, with a licensed guide. The ticket is mobile or paper, and cancellations are fully refunded up to 24 hours before departure.
 For a tight budget, the most effective lever is planning: book a visit early, choose screenings early in the day, and stay in the centre to limit travel. These are editorial tips, not figures from a source.
 8. A typical day at the festival
 A good day means fixing the visit and screenings in advance, then leaving room for the weather. Here is one possible plan, to adapt once the programme is published on 5 November.
 Morning: the guided tour of the museum and the Mole, which lasts two hours. If the weather allows, keep the panoramic climb for the end of the visit; if not, the visit may be limited to the museum.
 Early afternoon: one screening, preferably a less in-demand film, as popular screenings go quickly.
 Late afternoon: a walk through the historic centre, to get your bearings between screening venues and transport. Walking times were not checked.
 Evening: a second screening or free time, depending on the times confirmed by the organiser. Keep an alternative in case the first screening is full.
 This plan assumes a single day at the museum. If you stay several days, spread out screenings and activities, bearing in mind that the opening takes place at the Teatro Regio, whose time has not been published yet.
 9. By traveller type
 Film lover: wait for the programme on 5 November before choosing your screenings. The 2026 edition is dedicated to Marilyn Monroe, with a retrospective announced: a natural focus for your selection.
 First time in Turin: set aside a separate slot for the Mole and the museum, rather than squeezing them between two screenings.
 Tight budget: use the 2025 reduced ticket as a benchmark, and an indicative hostel bed from €20 a night. Skip the guided tour if the museum alone is enough for you.
 Journalist or photographer: the calendar is tight. The press accreditation request must be filed by Friday 30 October 2026 at 12:00 pm (time not confirmed by the organiser), and the fee is €60 before 3 November, €70 after.
 Reduced mobility: the Viator listing says the visit is not recommended for travellers with mobility problems. We found no accessibility information for the festival screening rooms. Contact the organiser before booking.
 10. Mistakes to avoid
 Buying on an unsourced 2026 price. No 2026 ticket price was published at this date: treat any figure shown without a dated source with caution.
 Aiming for a specific screening room without confirmation. Some online pages list the Cinema Massimo among the festival venues. The official programme, published on 5 November, will say which venues are confirmed.
 Booking a flight or a room without the official dates. The festival runs from 24 November to 2 December 2026, including the industry market if it concerns you.
 Relying on the panoramic climb without a backup. The Viator listing says it is not guaranteed in bad weather.
 Forgetting the 30 October deadline. For press coverage, this date matters more than any other: Friday 30 October 2026, 12:00 pm (time not confirmed by the organiser).
 What other guides don’t tell you
 The Hostelworld listing we checked repeats the festival dates. The points below, checked against official sources, do not appear in it.
 The press accreditation deadline is Friday 30 October 2026. The time given, 12:00 pm, is the one shown on the press page: the organiser has not confirmed it, so check it again before sending anything. The Hostelworld listing does not mention it. Source: press accreditation page (checked on 23 October 2026).
 The press fee is €60 before 3 November, €70 after. The Hostelworld listing does not mention it. Source: press accreditation page (checked on 23 October 2026).
 No 2026 ticket sales are published yet. The Hostelworld listing shows accommodation prices but no ticket prices. Source: 2025 ticketing information (checked on 23 October 2026).
 Not yet published: the opening ceremony time, the screening venues, the guest list and the film submission deadline. The programme will be presented in Rome on 5 November 2026. Source: torinofilmfest.org (checked on 23 October 2026).
 Practical information for planning your trip
 Practical 
 eSIM for Italy Mobile data from your arrival in Turin, with no physical SIM card. Plans vary by length: check the price on the page when you buy.
 Price depends on plan and duration 
Get my eSIM 
 Travel insurance: SafetyWing Useful for a short trip to Italy, especially if you hold non-refundable tickets. Cover depends on the plan: read the details before you buy.
 Price depends on plan and trip length 
Get covered 
 Frequently asked questions
 What are the dates of the Torino Film Festival 2026? The 44th edition runs from Tuesday 24 November to Wednesday 2 December 2026, nine days in all. The organiser confirms these dates on its official website, checked on 23 October 2026. The Torino Film Industry market is listed for 26 to 30 November by a secondary source, so treat it as unconfirmed until you check again before booking. torinofilmfest.org 
 Where is the opening ceremony held? The opening ceremony takes place at the Teatro Regio in Turin, hosted by the actress Ambra Angiolini, according to the organiser’s announcement. The start time had not been published at the check date, and access details, whether invitation or ticketing, have not been published either. Do not plan your arrival around a time that has not been confirmed.
 How much does a ticket cost in 2026? No 2026 price had been published as of 23 October 2026. In 2025, a full ticket cost €7.50, a reduced ticket €5.50 and the TFF Pass €110, according to the organiser’s ticketing information. These figures are a benchmark, not future prices. Check the official ticket office as soon as it opens.
 Do I need a visa to attend the festival? Not for British passport holders. A passport issued less than 10 years before arrival, and valid for at least three months after you leave the Schengen area, is enough for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period, according to the UK government’s travel advice for Italy, checked on 23 October 2026. Citizens of other countries should check their own government’s advice. gov.uk 
 When will the full programme be known? The full programme will be presented at a press conference in Rome on Thursday 5 November 2026, according to the official website checked on 23 October 2026. Before that date, the pages we checked list no detailed programme. Return to the organiser’s site afterwards for screenings and ticketing.
 What is the deadline for press accreditation? The deadline is Friday 30 October 2026 at 12:00 pm, according to the official press accreditation page; the organiser has not confirmed this time. The fee is €60 before 3 November and €70 after. The industry and photographer forms are on separate pages.
 How do I submit a film to the festival? We did not find the film submission deadline on an official source as of 23 October 2026. Read the regulations published by the organiser on torinofilmfest.org, and check the conditions there before you send anything.
 How many people attended the 43rd edition? About 38,000 attendances for 120 films in 2025, according to the final report relayed by Cinemaitaliano on 3 December 2025. That figure covers 2025 and does not predict attendance in 2026. The report also counts 65 sold-out screenings.
 Who are the guests of the Torino Film Festival 2026? The guest list had not been published as of 23 October 2026. The only name announced so far is Ambra Angiolini, who hosts the opening ceremony at the Teatro Regio, according to the organiser. The full list will come with the programme, presented in Rome on 5 November 2026.
 Sources
 Torino Film Festival, official site : dates, announced programme, dedication to Marilyn Monroe
 Opening ceremony of the 44th edition : venue and host
 2025 ticketing information : price references
 Press accreditation, 44th edition : deadline, fee, conditions
 Museo Nazionale del Cinema, festival lab : institutional home of the festival
 UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, Italy travel advice : entry and stay rules
 Cinemaitaliano, report on the 43rd edition : 2025 attendance
 Italy Meets Hollywood : market dates (secondary source)
 Product listing for the guided visit of the museum and the Mole, Viator API (checked 23 October 2026): duration, cancellation terms, reviews
 Hostelworld listing for the event: indicative accommodation, not linked to the festival
 Sources checked on 23 October 2026.
